source.title: The Shape of Beliefs: Geometry, Dynamics, and Interventions along Representation Manifolds of Language Models' Posteriors
source.authors: Raphael Sarfati; Eric J. Bigelow; Daniel Wurgaft; S. Boppana; Jack Merullo; Atticus Geiger; Owen Lewis; Tom McGrath; E. Lubana

record.tranche_reason: The study measures belief-representation geometry and argues that curved manifolds and multi-directional probe fields make single global linear directions an inadequate description. It does not test the original sparse-feature superposition setup.
record.gate_note: The paper studies posterior beliefs in numerical time-series prompts, not sparse overcomplete feature storage or interference. Probe accuracy and other results that do not bear on representational dimensionality are not included. Results cited from other work are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study does not test superposition. Its geometry results bear only on V6: a scalar latent (mean µ) in Llama-3.2-1B sits on a curved manifold. Its linear readout spans several directions (Gram-matrix rank >1), probes transfer only locally, and the (µ,σ) sheet is not an additive sum of the two anchor manifolds. This shows a multi-dimensional, not single-direction, feature representation. Whether these features are superposed is not examined.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that LLM posterior beliefs in this numerical task are encoded as curved manifolds, and that globally linear (single-direction) representations are often inadequate abstractions. Linear steering moves activations off-manifold and causes coupled shifts (e.g. in variance), while geometry-aware and LFP-based steering better preserve the belief family. They also stress that linear separability does not imply faithful linear control, especially when the probe field has rank >1.
record.recipe_differences: The study maps and intervenes on posterior-belief manifolds in a language model; it does not use the original toy-network feature-sparsity setup or measure superposition/interference.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported belief-manifold geometry varies across layers; the paper notes increasing intrinsic field dimensionality over layers except at the last layer. Field-aware steering preserves the target distribution only within a stated range.

fits_no_version.finding: Geometry-aware steering (manifold splines, LFP field steering) keeps outputs in the target N(µ,100) family better than linear steering, within roughly µ 300–500.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Interventions respecting representation-manifold geometry preserve the intended behaviour better than single-direction steering.

fits_no_version.finding: Mean µ is linearly decodable at all layers, with probe accuracy 0.87 at layer 0 rising to 0.99 at layer 15, despite the manifold's curvature.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Linear separability of a feature does not imply it is represented as a single linear direction.

record.problems: The study is constrained to numerical settings and base models without fine-tuning. The paper gives qualitative geometry and steering conclusions without uncertainty estimates for these findings, and does not test sparse overcomplete feature storage.

untested.parts: All of it: toy networks, sparsity-dependent transition, feature overlap and interference.
All of it: capacity competition and dedicated dimensions for important features.
All of it: no neuron-level polysemanticity analysis.
All of it: no neuron-distribution or SAE/dictionary analysis.
All of it: no SAE features examined.

Whether the multi-dimensional belief manifolds are stored in superposition with other features. Whether the finding extends beyond numerical distribution parameters, to non-base models, or to natural-language features.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked every row to V6 and scored states relative to curvature ('observed'). States are rescored against V6's 1-D-direction claim, so they become 'absent'. The verdict is limits_scope rather than challenges for two reasons: the paper never establishes that these belief features are superposed, and it concerns a narrow numerical setting. It therefore qualifies V6 without refuting it where V6 is defined. Comparator rows r16/r18 are the study's own method and are unlinked. Probe-accuracy rows r10/r11 are unlinked. The paper cites Toy Models of Superposition only as a reference for the linear representation hypothesis.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks with more sparse features than dimensions, sparsity-dependent transitions, overlap, interference, and regular feature geometry.
Whether polysemanticity results from capacity competition or important features receiving dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise for reasons other than capacity pressure.
Feature distribution across neurons in LLMs and sparse features recovered by dictionary learning or SAEs.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units of model representation.
The paper tests the geometry of numerical-belief representations, but does not test superposition of sparse features or establish that all model features are multidimensional.

rows.subject: Llama-3.2-1B
rows.operation_detail: PCA visualization of activations encoding normal-distribution beliefs

conditions.value: varying µ at σ=100; varying σ at µ=500

rows.value: The mean- and standard-deviation-indexed representations form smooth, continuous manifolds with substantial curvature; the paper describes the two manifolds as orthogonal.
rows.note: These are manifolds for the controlled numerical-belief task, not a test of sparse-feature superposition.
rows.check: State is recorded relative to curvature. Against V6 (1-D directions), the single-direction structure is absent: the text says the manifolds show 'substantial curvature' (Sec 3.1, Fig 1B).

source_check.correct: Smooth, substantially curved belief manifolds are observed. For V6 as written, state=cannot_determine and versions=[none]: the study does not establish that these manifolds are units stored in superposition.
source_check.problem: Curvature of belief representations does not establish absence of one-dimensional units in superposition.

rows.subject: LFM2-1.2B

conditions.value: after second layer, penultimate layer, last layer

rows.note: The authors state that qualitatively similar structured manifolds appear across the models shown.
rows.check: Evidence is only qualitative PCA plots (App B, Fig 9): 'qualitatively the same structured manifolds'. Curvature is not quantified for this model. The same caveat applies to r3–r9.

source_check.correct: Qualitatively structured manifolds are reported for LFM2-1.2B. State=cannot_determine and versions=[none] for V6; superposition is not measured.
source_check.problem: Qualitative PCA structure cannot establish absence of the effect specified by V6.

rows.subject: Llama-3.2-1B
rows.operation_detail: Train multiclass linear probes for discretized mean values
rows.note: Decodability alone does not establish whether the represented belief is one- or multi-dimensional.
rows.check: Linear-probe accuracy (0.87 at layer 0) measures decodability, not feature dimensionality or superposition. It should not be linked to V6.

rows.subject: Llama-3.2-1B
rows.operation_detail: Train multiclass linear probes for discretized mean values
rows.note: Decodability alone does not establish whether the represented belief is one- or multi-dimensional.
rows.check: Probe accuracy 0.99 at layer 15. Decodability only; not linked to V6.

rows.subject: Llama-3.2-1B
rows.operation_detail: Measure transfer of a probe trained at nearby mean values to more distant mean values
rows.baseline: An untrained binary probe has accuracy 0.5.
rows.value: Transfer is local and decays with distance in µ at a rate matching decay lengthscale in the Gram matrix.
rows.note: The text gives no individual transfer-accuracy values.
rows.check: Probes transfer only locally, which the authors say 'limits the validity of a single (global) linear direction'. Against V6 the 1-D-direction effect is absent. Values are figure-only (Fig 3D).

source_check.correct: Probe transfer is local and decays with distance in mean, matching the Gram-matrix decay lengthscale. State=cannot_determine and versions=[none] for V6; this tests global readout transfer, not the dimensionality of units established to be superposed.
source_check.problem: Local probe transfer limits a global readout direction without testing what is stored in superposition.

rows.subject: Llama-3.2-1B
rows.operation_detail: Examine eigenvalues of the linear-field-probe Gram matrix across layers
rows.measure: Intrinsic dimensionality of the linear readout field
rows.value: Intrinsic dimensionality increases over layers, with an exception at the last layer, where it drops.
rows.note: This measures field/readout dimensionality, not sparse-feature superposition.
rows.check: The readout field needs more than one direction, with intrinsic dimensionality rising over layers (Fig 4A). Against V6 the 1-D structure is absent. No numeric eigenvalues are given in the text.

source_check.correct: Readout-field dimensionality increases with depth and drops at the final layer. State=cannot_determine and versions=[none] for V6; the measured dimensionality concerns probe directions.
source_check.problem: Readout-field dimensionality is not the dimensionality of identified units in superposition.

rows.subject: Llama-3.2-1B
rows.operation_detail: Test additive interpolation of mean- and standard-deviation-anchored manifolds
rows.measure: Match between additively interpolated prototypes and ground-truth centroids
rows.baseline: Ground-truth centroids from activations for corresponding time series.
rows.value: The spline-based additive interpolation fails to capture the true geometry of the (µ, σ) sheet.
rows.note: The authors suggest nonlinear interactions between belief parameters as a possible explanation.
rows.check: Additive composition of the µ and σ manifolds fails (App E.4, Fig 13). This bears on whether features combine as simple independent directions. The evidence is qualitative.

source_check.correct: Spline-based additive interpolation from the anchored mean and standard-deviation manifolds fails to reproduce the joint sheet. State=cannot_determine and versions=[none] for V6; other decompositions remain possible.
source_check.problem: Failure of a particular additive decomposition does not determine the dimensionality of superposed units.

rows.subject: Llama-3.2-1B
rows.operation_detail: Add a centroid-to-centroid linear steering vector to activations
rows.measure: Shape of the induced next-token distribution
rows.value: Steered activations reaching µ=500 have a large variance and depart from N(500,100).
rows.note: The paper identifies this as linear steering cutting across a curved belief manifold.
rows.check: Centroid-difference linear steering leaves the belief family, consistent with a curved rather than single-direction representation. This is the baseline arm of the study's steering comparison.

source_check.correct: Centroid-difference steering produces excessive variance when the output mean reaches 500. State=cannot_determine and versions=[none] for V6; this is a steering comparison on a curved belief manifold.
source_check.problem: Off-manifold linear steering does not establish absence of one-dimensional units in superposition.

rows.subject: Llama-3.2-1B
rows.operation_detail: Steer along prototypes of the belief manifold
rows.measure: Shape of the induced next-token distribution
rows.value: Induced predictions remain close to N(µ,100) while shifting the mean toward 500.
rows.check: This is the study's own manifold-aware steering method compared against linear steering. It is a method-performance result, not a measure for any version.

rows.subject: Llama-3.2-1B
rows.operation_detail: Steer using the difference between endpoint linear probe vectors
rows.measure: Shape of the induced next-token distribution
rows.value: The single-probe-direction steering moves outputs away from the Gaussian manifold.
rows.note: The text does not report individual numerical distribution values.
rows.check: Steering along a single probe-difference direction moves outputs off the Gaussian family (Fig 6). The text wrongly references Fig. 4 here. Qualitative only.

source_check.correct: Steering along the normalized endpoint-probe difference moves outputs away from the Gaussian family. State=cannot_determine and versions=[none] for V6.
source_check.locator_found: Section 4.2, Linear probe steering; Figure 6 caption.
source_check.problem: A steering method's distribution distortion does not measure the dimensionality of superposed units.

rows.subject: Llama-3.2-1B
rows.operation_detail: Steer smoothly using the linear-field-probe geometry
rows.measure: Preservation of output standard deviation while changing mean
rows.value: The method maintains the same standard deviation while increasing the mean, at least in the stated range.
rows.note: Comparator to steering along a single probe direction.
rows.check: This is the study's own LFP field-aware steering method compared against single-direction steering. It is method performance, not a version measure.

relationships.condition: Llama-3.2-1B, mean/std of in-context Gaussian time series, com2num tokens
relationships.reason: Several results show the µ feature is a curved, multi-directional manifold rather than a single direction. These are the curved manifold (r1), local-only probe transfer (r12), readout rank >1 rising with layers (r13), non-additive (µ,σ) composition (r14), and linear steering going off-manifold (r15, r17). Superposition itself is not tested.
relationships.display_finding: The µ feature lay on a curved manifold: probes transferred only locally, readout rank exceeded one and rose with layers, (µ, σ) composition was non-additive, and linear steering went off-manifold. Superposition itself was not tested.

labels.label: limits_scope
labels.condition: Eight further base models (LFM2, LFM2.5, Llama-3.1/3.2, OLMo-2/3), PCA at three layers
labels.reason: Rows r2–r9 provide qualitative evidence of structured belief manifolds, without identifying superposed units or measuring their dimensionality. They do not test V6 as written.

relation.reason: The paper discusses linear feature representations and additive superposition, but its own results do not determine the dimensionality of units shown to be stored in superposition.

tranche.reason: The study tests belief-manifold geometry, readout and steering. It does not establish superposition of the observed manifolds, so it does not test V6 as written or another listed version. Appendix E.4's additive-manifold hypothesis concerns a related representational construct.

source_check.notes: The reported empirical findings and conditions are accurate. The central correction is to distinguish evidence against globally linear belief representations from evidence about the units stored in superposition; encoding, readout-field and intrinsic manifold dimensions also differ.

statements.correction: Llama-3.2-1B: curved Gaussian-belief manifolds; local probe transfer; multidirectional readout fields; failed anchored additive composition. Additional base models: qualitative structured-manifold PCA results. Superposition of these manifolds with other features: untested.
statements.problem: The empirical description is accurate, but its limits_scope classification for V6 exceeds the evidence: the study does not identify these belief manifolds as superposed units.

statements.correction: Representation geometry and steering are measured. Storage of the observed manifolds in superposition with other features is not established. Appendix E.4 tests a particular additive decomposition and allows other decompositions.
statements.problem: The evidential distinction is correct. However, this paper does not explicitly formulate the specific open question of whether its recovered manifolds are stored in superposition with other features.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Numerical-belief representations in Llama-3.2-1B and the additional models shown in Appendix B
reader_labels.reason: The tested representations include curved manifolds, locally transferring probes, increasing field dimensionality, and failed additive manifold interpolation; linear steering also leaves the intended belief family (r1-r9, r12-r18).
